Topical application of tea tree oil (TTO) can cause significant ocular toxicity. A case report documented corneal epithelial defects resulting from the use of a 50% TTO solution for blepharitis, leading to conjunctival injection and corneal epithelial defects that required intensive treatment with lubricants, antibiotics, steroids, and bandage contact lenses to facilitate healing.[1] Additionally, in vitro studies have shown that TTO concentrations exceeding 0.01% significantly reduce the viability of corneal keratocytes, with concentrations of 0.1% or higher inducing apoptotic cell death.[2]. Given these findings, it is crucial to avoid direct application of TTO to the ocular surface. When using TTO for conditions like blepharitis, it should be in very low concentrations and applied with caution to avoid contact with the eyes. 1.
